l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable

q: Minerva took the head of her once beautiful rival and placed it in the middle of her Aegis.

s: monsters is a beings of unnatural proportions or parts (in mythology)
q: Monsters, in the language of mythology, were beings of unnatural proportions or parts, usually regarded with terror, as possessing immense strength and ferocity, which they employed for the injury and annoyance of men.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Chimaera is a fire-breathing monster
q: The Chimaera was a fearful monster, breathing fire.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Chimaera has body parts lion, goat, and dragon (fore part lion and goat; hind part dragon)
q: The fore part of its body was a compound of the lion and the goat, and the hind part a dragon's.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Centaurs is a half-man, half-horse people (men to the waist and horses below)
q: But nobler and better were the Centaurs, men to the waist, while the rest was the form of a horse.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Centaurs are admitted to companionship of man
q: The Centaurs were admitted to the companionship of man, and at the marriage of Pirithous with Hippodamia, they were among the guests.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Centaurs fight Lapithae (in the battle of the Lapithae and Centaurs)
q: This is the celebrated battle of the Lapithae and Centaurs, a favorite subject with the sculptors and poets of antiquity.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Griffin is a lion-eagle monster (with eagle head and wings)
q: The Griffin is a monster with the body of a lion, the head and wings of an eagle, and back covered with feathers.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Griffin builds nests gold (in India)
q: India was assigned as the native country of the Griffins. They found gold in the mountains and built their nests of it, for which reason their nests were very tempting to the hunters, and they were forced to keep vigilant guard over them.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Griffin guards buried treasures (by keeping plunderers away)
q: Their instinct led them to know where buried treasures lay, and they did their best to keep plunderers at a distance.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pygmies is a nation of dwarfs (about thirteen inches tall)
q: The Pygmies were a nation of dwarfs, so called from a Greek word which means the cubit (a cubit was a measure of about thirteen inches), which was said to be the height of these people.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: monsters possess immense strength and ferocity (typically)
q: Monsters, in the language of mythology, were beings of unnatural proportions or parts, usually regarded with terror, as possessing immense strength and ferocity, which they employed for the injury and annoyance of men.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pygmies live near Nile (according to one account)
q: They lived near the sources of the Nile, or according to others, in India.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pygmies fight cranes (to defend their cornfields)
q: Homer tells us that the cranes used to migrate every winter to the Pygmies' country, and their appearance was the signal of bloody warfare to the puny inhabitants, who had to take up arms to defend their cornfields against the rapacious strangers.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Cyclopes is a human giants (not altogether disproportioned to humans)
q: The human giants, if so they may be called, such as the Cyclopes, Antaeus, Orion, and others, must be supposed not to be altogether disproportioned to human beings, for they mingled in love and strife with them.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Typhon breathes fire (as a giant)
q: Some of them, like Briareus, had a hundred arms; others, like Typhon, breathed out fire.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Jupiter takes form of ram (when the gods flee to Egypt)
q: Jupiter took the form of a ram, whence he was afterwards worshipped in Egypt as the god Ammon, with curved horns.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Minerva invents thunderbolts (for Jupiter)
q: They were at last subdued by thunderbolts, which Minerva invented, and taught Vulcan and his Cyclopes to make for Jupiter.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: the giants is a monsters (differing chiefly from men in size)
q: Others, as the giants, differed from men chiefly in their size; and in this particular we must recognize a wide distinction among them.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Laius is a king of Thebes
q: Laius, king of Thebes, was warned by an oracle that there was danger to his throne and life if his new-born son should be suffered to grow up.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: herdsman (Laius's agent) spares OEdipus (out of pity)
q: but the herdsman, moved to pity, yet not daring entirely to disobey, tied up the child by the feet, and left him hanging to the branch of a tree.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Polybus adopts OEdipus (with Merope)
q: Polybus and Merope, his wife, adopted the child, whom they called OEdipus, or Swollen-foot, for they had no children themselves, and in Corinth OEdipus grew up.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Merope is wife of Polybus
q: Polybus and Merope, his wife, adopted the child, whom they called OEdipus, or Swollen-foot, for they had no children themselves, and in Corinth OEdipus grew up.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: OEdipus is a king of Thebes (after solving the Sphinx's riddle)
q: The gratitude of the people for their deliverance was so great that they made OEdipus their king, giving him in marriage their queen Jocasta.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: OEdipus solves Sphinx's riddle (answering man)
q: OEdipus replied, "Man, who in childhood creeps on hands and knees, in manhood walks erect, and in old age with the aid of a staff."

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: OEdipus is husband of Jocasta (unknowingly his mother)
q: in marrying the queen he became the husband of his mother.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: OEdipus loses eyesight blindness (after the double crime is revealed)
q: Jocasta put an end to her own life, and OEdipus, seized with madness, tore out his eyes, and wandered away from Thebes, dreaded and abandoned hy all except his daughters, who faithfully adhered to him; till after a tedious period of miserable wandering, he found the termination of his wretched life.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: the giants war with Olympian gods (in the war of the giants against the gods)
q: We have already spoken of the war which the giants waged against the gods, and of its result.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pegasus is a winged horse (born from Medusa's blood)
q: When Perseus cut off Medusa's head, the blood sinking into the earth produced the winged horse Pegasus.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pegasus belongs to Muses (presented by Minerva)
q: Minerva caught and tamed him, and presented him to the Muses.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Pegasus creates Hippocrene (with a kick of his hoof)
q: The fountain Hippocrene, on the Muses' mountain Helicon, was opened by a kick from his hoof.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Iobates is a king of Lycia
q: It made great havoc in Lycia, so that the king Iobates sought for some hero to destroy it.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Iobates assigns Chimaera (as a deadly trial for Bellerophon)
q: A lucky thought occurred to him, to send Bellerophon to combat with the Chimaera.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Bellerophon defeats Chimaera (riding Pegasus)
q: Bellerophon mounting, rose with him into the air, and soon found the Chimaera, and gained an easy victory over the monster.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Bellerophon marries Iobates's daughter (after completing his trials)
q: After the conquest of the Chimaera, Bellerophon was exposed to further trials and labors by his unfriendly host, but by the aid of Pegasus he triumphed in them all; till at length Iobates, seeing that the hero was a special favorite of the gods, gave him his daughter in marriage and made him his successor on the throne.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Bellerophon is punished by Olympian gods (for pride and presumption)
q: At last Bellerophon by his pride and presumption drew upon himself the anger of the gods; it is said he even attempted to fly up into heaven on his winged steed; but Jupiter sent a gadfly which stung Pegasus and made him throw his rider, who became lame and blind in consequence.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Chiron is a Centaur (wisest and justest of all)
q: Chiron was the wisest and justest of all the Centaurs, and at his death Jupiter placed him among the stars as the constellation Sagittarius.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: the giants attempt to reach heaven (by piling mountains)
q: At another time the giants attempted to climb up into heaven, and for that purpose took up the mountain Ossa and piled it on Pelion.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Chiron teaches Aesculapius (among many heroic pupils)
q: The most distinguished heroes of Grecian story were his pupils. Among the rest the infant Aesculapius was intrusted to his charge, by Apollo, his father.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Chiron becomes Sagittarius (after death)
q: Chiron was the wisest and justest of all the Centaurs, and at his death Jupiter placed him among the stars as the constellation Sagittarius.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Aesculapius is a physician (renowned and capable of restoring the dead)
q: Aesculapius, when grown up, became a renowned physician, and even in one instance succeeded in restoring the dead to life.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable

q: Pluto resented this, and Jupiter, at his request, struck the bold physician with lightning and killed him, but after his death received him into the number of the gods.

q: But the hero awaking laughed at the little warriors, wrapped some of them up in his lion's-skin, and carried them to Eurystheus.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Sphinx is a monster (with human and leonine parts)
q: It was called the Sphinx. It had the body of a lion, and the upper part of a woman.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Sphinx infests Thebes (on the high-road)
q: Shortly after this event the city of Thebes was afflicted with a monster which infested the high-road. It was called the Sphinx.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Sphinx poses Sphinx's riddle (to travelers on the road)
q: It lay crouched on the top of a rock, and stopped all travellers who came that way, proposing to them a riddle, with the condition that those who could solve it should pass safe, but those who failed should be killed.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Sphinx dies by self-destruction (after OEdipus solves its riddle)
q: The Sphinx was so mortified at the solving of her riddle that she cast herself down from the rock and perished.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable

q: Phryxus sacrificed the ram to Jupiter, and gave the golden fleece to AEetes, who placed it in a consecrated grove, under the care of a sleepless dragon.

q: the girl, whose name was Helle, fell from his back into the sea, which from her was called the Hellespont, now the Dardanelles.

q: who was hospitably received by AEetes, the king of the country.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: dragon (guardian of the Golden Fleece) guards Golden Fleece (in a consecrated grove and without sleeping)
q: Phryxus sacrificed the ram to Jupiter, and gave the golden fleece to AEetes, who placed it in a consecrated grove, under the care of a sleepless dragon.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable

q: Hercules, Theseus, Orpheus, and Nestor were among them.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Greeks include Nestor (among the Argonauts)
q: Hercules, Theseus, Orpheus, and Nestor were among them.

l: Bulfinch's Mythology: The Age of Fable
s: Phineus is a sage sage
q: Here they found the sage Phineus, and from him received instruction as to their future course.
